Does anyone think this is a problem (e.g. too much boilerplate)? I've seen voices asking to make everything optional (e.g. having data section only). What are the odds that if the code_section == Nil, we can place a single opcode in there like INVALID or NOOP. My rationale is that we maximize benefits from standardized checks across the container format without losing flexibility this will require extra bytes that are useless also in what context the data_section gets used ? Three bytes to explicitly say "no data." Less conditionals also simplifies the parser logic which unlocks some optimization options. However a simpler parser is better for reference implementations. hello all, being `RJUMPI` and `RJUMPV` the first opcodes to cost 4 gas, would make sense to name a new tier for them? we already have _base_, _verylow_, _low_, _mid_ and _high_, and these two would be between verylow and low in the EIP-3670 spec, it says `Previously deprecated instructions CALLCODE (0xf2) and SELFDESTRUCT (0xff) are invalid and their opcodes are undefined.` when were these opcode deprecated ? Hi guys, question, does this test assume that `3860` is enabled. for us it when running the test called `stEIP3540.CREATE_EOF1_d4g0v0_deploying_0xef_Merge+3540+3670)` because when we run it with `3860` enabled, it fails because it is deducting gas for metering InitCode <@450651770243252225> might have similar issues. <@543900561460822016> <@425269142615097345> <@425279588009246720> <@425274498732916736><@403707149043105803> Looking at the criteria as per prior ACD: -------- https://twitter.com/TimBeiko/status/1600945407852703744 Criteria for EOF inclusion in Shanghai: "1. By the next AllCoreDevs (Jan 5, 2023), we want to have all clients with a complete EOF implementation and passing test suites. 2. By the ACD after that (Jan 19, 2023), we want to have seen EL clients interop on a devnet. If these bars aren't met, then EOF will be removed." -------- .... Do we have a clear and objective measure as to what "passing test suites" really means? How extensive must those tests be? Those are only per-client tests? Or should include ethereum/tests? Shandong syncing status unimportant for that test? If we are in a place where, for example, perhaps we have Geth, Erigon and Besu "done" and Nethermind not quite done, is that an "abort mission"? That is a hard line, **all clients**? (not picking on Nethermind specifically here, btw - could be any of clients being not quite there but very close) Status: https://notes.ethereum.org/@ipsilon/eof1-checklist More general, what is the status on creation of a full EOF testnet? Or we waiting on withdrawals to be complete and then just having a combined testnet? What is the plan? Thanks! Also, i am facing issues with tests that have `initcode` that returns `code` that is not eof and the test assumes this is valid. as per this validation in the EIP, it should not be valid. Eip states: ``` If initcode’s container is valid EOF1 code the resulting code’s container MUST be valid EOF1 code (i.e. it MUST NOT be empty and MUST NOT produce legacy code). ``` Feeling like Ethereum tests are still not ready. is there a specific time that the Ethereum tests will be finalized? ^^ <@393119312350543872> Also as per EIP-3670 `callcode` should be deprecated. it states: ``` Previously deprecated instructions CALLCODE (0xf2) and SELFDESTRUCT (0xff) are invalid and their opcodes are undefined. ``` when we deprecate `CALLCODE` we fail some ethereum tests To summarize we have 3 pending issues with Ethereum tests: 1. 3860 gas deduction fails tests 2. `Initcode` that return `code` that is not EOF is assumed valid in tests. when the check is enabled tests fail 3. callcode deprecation fails tests Which tests are you running? Eof tests are in GeneralStateTests/EIPTests/stEOF <@275684146658148352> developed most of it The init code tests are in development https://github.com/ethereum/tests/pull/1112 CALLCODE is a broken opcode supplanted by DELEGATECALL. Deprecating SELFDESTRUCT is to support the widly held desire to remove it for stuff like verkle. If we do need it it's easier to re-add it, removing it requires a major EOF version bump, so we are trying to get in as much as we can. I know but the Eip3760 spec states that it was previously deprecated, which to my understanding means another Eip is taking care of that, also EthereumTests seem to ignore this.

excerpts.author: bobsummerwill
excerpts.content:
<@543900561460822016> <@425269142615097345> <@425279588009246720> <@425274498732916736><@403707149043105803> 

Looking at the criteria as per prior ACD:

--------
https://twitter.com/TimBeiko/status/1600945407852703744

Criteria for EOF inclusion in Shanghai:

"1. By the next AllCoreDevs (Jan 5, 2023), we want to have all clients with a complete EOF implementation and passing test suites. 
2. By the ACD after that (Jan 19, 2023), we want to have seen EL clients interop on a devnet. 

If these bars aren't met, then EOF will be removed."
--------

.... Do we have a clear and objective measure as to what "passing test suites" really means?    How extensive must those tests be?  Those are only per-client tests?  Or should include ethereum/tests?  Shandong syncing status unimportant for that test?

If we are in a place where, for example, perhaps we have Geth, Erigon and Besu "done" and Nethermind not quite done, is that an "abort mission"?  That is a hard line, **all clients**?    (not picking on Nethermind specifically here, btw - could be any of clients being not quite there but very close)

Status:
https://notes.ethereum.org/@ipsilon/eof1-checklist

More general, what is the status on creation of a full EOF testnet?   Or we waiting on withdrawals to be complete and then just having a combined testnet?    What is the plan?  Thanks!

excerpts.author: smartprogrammer
excerpts.content:
Also, i am facing issues with tests that have `initcode` that returns `code` that is not eof and the test assumes this is valid. 
as per this validation in the EIP, it should not be valid.
Eip states:
```
If initcode’s container is valid EOF1 code the resulting code’s container MUST be valid EOF1 code (i.e. it MUST NOT be empty and MUST NOT produce legacy code).
```
Feeling like Ethereum tests are still not ready. is there a specific time that the Ethereum tests will be finalized?

excerpts.author: smartprogrammer
excerpts.content:
Also as per EIP-3670 `callcode` should be deprecated. it states:
```
Previously deprecated instructions CALLCODE (0xf2) and SELFDESTRUCT (0xff) are invalid and their opcodes are undefined.
```
when we deprecate `CALLCODE` we fail some ethereum tests

2. `Initcode` that return `code` that is not EOF is assumed valid in tests. when the check is enabled tests fail
3. callcode deprecation fails tests
